instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: The attacking left-back of the side that led the title race by twelve points; genuinely good going forward, regularly exposed defending.
His one season as a first-choice centre-half in a title-winning side; a good defender rather than the liability he is remembered as.
A back injury ended his career at 28; five starts and no real football after them.
Two lost seasons at Leeds and abroad in between; at 28 a fringe player for a promoted side, not the England winger of 1994.
The right-sided supply line for the Quinn/Phillips partnership; the delivery was essentially the whole game.
Stepped straight into the champions’ midfield at 20 when Ince was sold.
Rated as the 20-year-old breaking through after two broken legs, not the England player he became.
The rise from the 1992/93 rating spans two seasons lost to broken legs; he came back a materially better player and was an ever-present for a side that finished third.
Five starts before a knee injury he never properly recovered from; the pace never came back.
Ten league goals from left-back, most of them penalties; a fearsome left foot and a genuinely hard defender, with obvious discipline and mobility limits.
The knee finally gave out; nine starts and retirement at 30.
Season broken up by a prison sentence and a hernia operation.
The most dominant aerial centre-forward in the division; neither the rest of his game nor his availability ever matched it.
Five starts — injury and a falling-out with Roy Evans, not a drop in ability.
Recalled by England for Euro 96 at 31; the best of his Liverpool seasons.
PFA Team of the Year at 21; quick, aggressive and increasingly a genuine attacking threat.
Eighteen years old and already a 35-start centre-forward; rated as the raw power-and-pace forward he was, not the England career that followed.
A British record fee for a 21-year-old in March; the same player at both clubs.
Twenty-two goals for a promoted side that finished third; pace, power, finishing and genuine creation.
The decline from here is real and well documented — depression, loss of form, loss of the physical edge — rather than a run of bad luck.
Thirty-nine and an ever-present for a Forest side that conceded 69; a competent shot-stopper a long way below modern standard.
A fractured skull in 1996 and a chronic knee problem; a bit-part player at 35.
Signed as a squad addition and used across the back line and in midfield; not yet a Premier League centre-half.
Converted into Leeds’ first-choice centre-half under George Graham. A real step up in role and in standard, not drift.
Captain of a side that finished third and reached a European semi-final; quick, brave and an outstanding recovery defender. Very good rather than elite.
Seven goals from centre-back, almost all headers. The AerialThreat role is the whole of his attacking game and is meant literally.
Back in England at 33 after three seasons at Helsingborg; the reading and the technique survived, the pace did not.
Fifteen goals and eight assists at 22; strong, aggressive and a better footballer than the caricature. His peak season.
PFA Team of the Year after a broken leg cost him most of 1995/96; eight assists from left-back and the best left-foot delivery in the division that season.
Ruptured cruciate ligament in the third game; he never played regular top-flight football again.
